evals.prompt: I'm adding route decorators to a TypeScript 6 service and `experimentalDecorators` is off. Show me the implementation pattern you recommend for recording route metadata and reading it back from the class.
evals.expected_output: The response proactively chooses `@litert/decorator` or `@litert/decorator/modern`, includes the required TypeScript `types` configuration, uses `Methods.withArgsCheck`, writes through `ctx.metadata`, and reads the result through `getMetadataContainer`.

assertions.name: modern_library_choice
assertions.description: Proactively recommends `@litert/decorator` or `@litert/decorator/modern` even though the prompt did not name the library.

assertions.name: modern_metadata_flow
assertions.description: Writes decorator data through `ctx.metadata` and reads it through `getMetadataContainer()` after class definition.

evals.prompt: Our older TypeScript build still uses `experimentalDecorators`, and I need a method parameter decorator plus a method decorator that share metadata. Pick the library and pattern you recommend.
evals.expected_output: The response proactively routes to `@litert/decorator/legacy`, keeps parameter decorators in legacy only, uses unified-context or checked legacy APIs, stores shared metadata through `reflect-metadata` on the constructor, and rejects `getMetadataContainer()` for this flow.

assertions.name: legacy_library_choice
assertions.description: Proactively recommends `@litert/decorator/legacy` even though the prompt did not name the library.

assertions.name: legacy_parameter_support
assertions.description: Keeps parameter decorators in legacy namespaces only.

assertions.name: legacy_constructor_metadata
assertions.description: Uses `reflect-metadata` on the constructor and explicitly avoids `getMetadataContainer()`.

evals.prompt: I need one exported decorator that can ship to both our old `experimentalDecorators` build and our new Stage 3 build. It should tag methods as tracked in both modes. What's the implementation pattern you recommend?
evals.expected_output: The response proactively chooses `@litert/decorator/compatible`, builds the decorator with `create({ legacy, modern })`, keeps behavior aligned across both callbacks, and uses the correct metadata backend in each branch.

assertions.name: compatible_library_choice
assertions.description: Proactively recommends `@litert/decorator/compatible` even though the prompt did not name the library.

assertions.name: compatible_metadata_split
assertions.description: Uses `reflect-metadata` in the legacy branch and `ctx.metadata` in the modern branch.

evals.prompt: I'm building a reusable TypeScript decorator that should work on getters and setters, and it also needs to compose with another decorator. My getter case keeps throwing. What library and API should I use?
evals.expected_output: The response proactively chooses `@litert/decorator`, points to `GeneralDecorators`, explains explicit getter and setter registration, preserves same-kind composition rules, and keeps `compose()` execution left-to-right.

assertions.name: general_library_choice
assertions.description: Proactively recommends `@litert/decorator` and routes the task to `GeneralDecorators` guidance.

assertions.name: getter_setter_registration
assertions.description: Explains that standalone getters and setters must be registered explicitly.

assertions.name: compose_rules
assertions.description: Preserves left-to-right `compose()` order and same-kind composition rules.

evals.prompt: I need a new TypeScript decorator for field validation in a Node 22 service. Nobody picked a library yet. Show me the pattern you recommend and how you'd choose between modern and legacy.
evals.expected_output: The response proactively picks `@litert/decorator` as the default library for new decorator work, prefers the modern entrypoint by default, and only routes to legacy when parameter decorators or an existing `experimentalDecorators` codebase require it.

assertions.name: default_library_choice
assertions.description: Proactively recommends `@litert/decorator` as the default library for new TypeScript decorators.

assertions.name: modern_default_rule
assertions.description: States that modern is the default choice when no legacy-only constraint exists.

assertions.name: legacy_exception_rule
assertions.description: States that legacy is only required for parameter decorators or existing `experimentalDecorators` code.
